Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: George Eliot (author, Wikidata Q131333), died 1880; Elizabeth Barrett Browning (author, Wikidata Q228494), died 1861; Robert Browning (author, Wikidata Q233265), died 1889; Percy Bysshe Shelley (author, Wikidata Q93343), died 1822. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Eliot, George, 1819-1880; Browning, Elizabeth Barrett, 1806-1861; Browning, Robert, 1812-1889; Shelley, Percy Bysshe, 1792-1822") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: O may I join the choir invisible!, Boston, D. Lothrop and company, 1884, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/omayijoinchoirin00elio. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 93%, 63%, 56% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of George Eliot, Elizabeth Barrett Browning, Robert Browning, Percy Bysshe Shelley, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
